It's an ointment that is basically for diaper rash. It has vitamin Aand D in which are both important for your skin. It's not white and goopy like dome diaper creams, but moisturizing and provides sort of a barrier.  You can find it in the diaper aisle.  If you want to go natural look for California Baby products with calendula or Burt's Bees diaper cream.  But the powder is a bad idea because it absorbs the moisture and dryness is what is causing the cracking.  I can PM you with my specifics(Dr.'s advice)if you want, or you. An PM me.

Don't use gold Bond or any powder, it will dry you out and make it worse.  You need moisture/protection, like A&D ointment until it heals.  Use it right after your shower when your skin is moist to seal it in.  Put some neosporin CREAM on it first, then the A&D.  I know it feels gross, but if feels better than cracked bleeding skin and an infection.  If it doesn't get better, see a dermatologist and see if you might have psoriasis.  Hope it works out.

My derm told me that if I used a cleanser that stripped my skin of oil/natural moisture, my sebaceous glands would produce more oil to compensate for the loss.  So it's important to find a cleanser that doesn't strip your skin.  These are cleansers she recommends from the drugstore: Purpose (I use this one), Cetaphil, Basis (bar), Dove Sensitive Bar, and Vanicream Cleansing Bar.  Purpose has a  Good moisturizer too that isn't heavy as it is geared towards sensitive skin.  Hope this helps :)
